jurisdiction.name: Suriname
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Suriname has no national AI law, strategy or official AI guidance. The economic affairs and technological innovation ministry (EZOTI) began a UNESCO AI readiness assessment in August 2026, and a privacy and personal data protection bill that would give a right against solely automated decisions is still pending before the National Assembly. The National Digital Strategy 2023-2030 mentions AI only as a trend.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation (EZOTI)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the National Assembly's and the central government portal's websites; all were reachable. The pending privacy bill, the UNESCO readiness assessment and a responsible-AI policy for government that has been announced are tracked as leads.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Suriname's National Assembly bill and law lists, the central government portal, ministries and regulators were searched, and no qualifying AI-governance document was found in any category. A pending privacy bill and the National Digital Strategy 2023-2030 are listed as leads. Not yet verified from the official text: when the privacy bill was submitted and its current stage.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. dna.sr bill lists (submitted, in progress, approved) and laws list scanned; no separate online gazette search. gov.sr search API in Dutch and English. Penal Code amendment bill 2022 (scan) only changes fine categories. Privacy bill pending in National Assembly (lead per bills-in-parliament rule); submission date unstated (secondary: 2018). National Digital Strategy 2023-2030: AI as trend only (scope test). CBvS AI item found in discovery is Philippine (excluded). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: The National Assembly site (dna.sr) bill lists (submitted, in progress, approved) and its Surinaamse wetten list were searched. No AI law or AI provision is in force. The Privacy and Personal Data Protection bill, which includes an automated-decision/profiling right, is still pending ('In behandeling') and is held as a lead. The submitted Penal Code amendment bill (agenda no. 1802/22, August 2022) was read (scanned PDF) and only changes fine categories. Art. 307a of the Penal Code (S.B. 2020 no. 42) on shocking images is not AI-specific. There is no separate online Staatsblad search portal; gazette references were checked through dna.sr and gov.sr. Searched; no in-scope law found.; Government: Searched gov.sr (central government portal), including the Kabinet van de President, the Directorate e-Government and EZOTI news. No national AI strategy, AI governance framework, public-sector AI guideline or GenAI guidance has been published. Activity found was workshops and trainings in 2025-2026, AI Impact Summit participation in February 2026, and the start of the UNESCO RAM in August 2026. The National Digital Strategy 2023-2030 has no AI pillar and is held as a lead. Searched, nothing in scope found.; Ministries: Searched gov.sr news and documents from EZOTI, Education (OWC, statements on AI misuse by pupils, June 2026, no policy document), Justice and Police (no AI rule), TCT (Electronic Communications Act revision announced), BIBIS (AI chatbot, no guidance), Health, Finance, Labour and Defence. No ministry-level AI document was found.; Regulators: Checked the Central Bank of Suriname (cbvs.sr), which has no AI guidance; an AI-in-finance principles item found in discovery is from the Philippines, not Suriname. There is no data protection authority (one is proposed in the pending privacy bill). No AI-specific documents were found from the telecom authority (TAS), a cyber agency or the standards bureau (SSB; only a 2024 World Standards Day panel news item). Searched, nothing found.. Not reached: none. Could not verify: When the privacy bill was submitted and its exact current stage: neither the DNA page nor the bill text states a date (secondary sources say it was submitted in 2018 and discussed in committee in January 2021).; Convention 108: Suriname is not known to be a party, and no ratification or accession act was found on dna.sr or gov.sr.. binding-law, strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.title: Wet Bescherming Privacy en Persoonsgegevens (ontwerpwet)
leads.english_title: Privacy and Personal Data Protection Act (bill)
leads.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Suriname (bill before De Nationale Assemblée)
leads.note: Pending bill, listed under 'In behandeling' on the National Assembly's site (https://www.dna.sr/wetgeving/ontwerpwetten-bij-dna/in-behandeling/ontwerpwet-bescherming-privacy-en-persoonsgegevens/; text marked ONTWERP: https://www.dna.sr/media/2w5lbamt/wet_bescherming_privacy_en_persoonsgegevens.pdf, read via curl). It defines profiling and gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with legal or similarly significant effects; the explanatory memorandum names AI-driven profiling as an example. It would create an independent Commissaris voor persoonsgegevensbescherming. No submission or adoption date is stated on the DNA page or in the text; no enacted version found. Record as binding_law (data-privacy) once adopted and published in the Staatsblad.

leads.title: National Digital Strategy 2023 - 2030
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Suriname (Presidential Working Group on e-Government / Directorate e-Government)
leads.note: Official document on gov.sr (https://gov.sr/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Suriname-National-Digital-Strategy-2023-2030.pdf, read via curl/pdftotext); the document states only the year 2023 ('© Government of Suriname, 2023'). Out of scope as a record: AI appears only as a trend in the foreword and sector analyses (education, health, public services, agriculture, oil and gas); its six priorities and roadmap contain no AI pillar or AI action. Its roadmap does call for developing or strengthening the privacy and data-protection legal framework.

leads.title: UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment (RAM) for Suriname
leads.english_title: UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment (RAM 2.0) for Suriname
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation (EZOTI) with UNESCO
leads.note: An assessment process, not yet a document. It was reported to have started with a stakeholder meeting on 27 August 2026, led by EZOTI; no government notice or report was found on gov.sr. EZOTI's permanent secretary for technological innovation is reported to be preparing a national AI strategy. Record the RAM country report or the AI strategy once published officially.

leads.title: Beleid en richtlijnen voor verantwoord AI-gebruik binnen de overheid
leads.english_title: Policy and guidelines for responsible AI use in government (announced)
leads.note: Announcement of intent only. At an AI awareness session on 30 April 2025, the e-Gov director said the government would examine whether policy and guidelines for responsible AI use in government are needed (gov.sr news item 'Nieuwe e-visa-applicatie en chatbot gelanceerd tijdens AI-bewustwordingssessie'). No document has been found.
